summary: 54-ft fire lookout that served Kinderlou Forest 1939-1993; donated to the state and, per 2012 and 2016 sources, stands at the Grand Bay Wetland Education Center.

facts.status_note: Sources (2012 essay, 2016 encyclopedia entry) place it at the Grand Bay Wetland Education Center. They do not say whether it was moved from its fire-lookout site, or when.

access.note: The Grand Bay Wetland Education Center offers the boardwalk and interpretive experience to the public. A 2012 essay said a Georgia Outdoor Recreation Pass was then required.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile boardwalk ends at the tower. A 2012 essay warned that red wasps nest on the structure in summer.

facts.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources and Coastal Plains Regional Educational Service Agency, partners who operate the Grand Bay Wetland Education Center

events.note: Served as a fire lookout in nearby Kinderlou Forest from 1939, per a 2012 photo essay.
The same essay gives 1993 as the end of its fire-lookout service.

notes_for_editor: Index has two Kinderlou entries: GA097 'kinderlou' (30.79958, -83.35439, 213 ft) and GA232 'old kinderlou' (30.79228, -83.36838, 234 ft, this record), about 1.6 km apart. The index says names for towers 73 and up are its author's own, so the names are not official. This record's point is about 24 km from the Wikipedia coordinates for Grand Bay (30.93472, -83.17333), so it may mark the original Kinderlou Forest site rather than the tower at Grand Bay. The story describes the Grand Bay tower, which the 2012 essay and encyclopedia entry support; no source links this index row to that tower. Not verified against a map; no coordinates for the current tower were found. Sources do not date the move or the donation, so no relocated event is recorded. Do not confuse with the NHLR 'Lowndes County Fire Tower' (US 1474, GA 28), a 100-ft steel tower near Delmar, built 1937 and still in use, which is a different structure. Access and pass details come from a 2012 essay; check current rules before publishing. Brief elevation (71.3 m) matches the index's 234 only if read as feet; the index gives no unit.
